title: My Life Experiences: Things I've Done and Haven't Done Yet
writingModel: My Life Experiences — by Zhibek Akhmetova

When I think about the experiences I've had, I realise they have mostly been shaped by two things: volleyball and curiosity. These two forces have taken me to places I never expected to go — both physically and intellectually.

I've represented Kazakhstan in international competitions twice. I went to Bishkek in 2022 and to Tashkent in 2023. In both cases, the level was higher than anything I had faced before. I didn't win, but I have never regretted going. Those tournaments taught me more about resilience than any training session ever could.

I've also written two research papers. The first was a study of how Kazakh athletes manage stress before competitions. The second — which has just been accepted for publication — examines training methods used in elite volleyball programmes. I never expected to enjoy academic writing, but I've discovered that I love it. The structure, the precision, the challenge of saying something new.

There are many things I haven't done yet. I've never won the national volleyball championship. That is still my biggest goal. I haven't visited more than five countries. I haven't learned a third language — my Kazakh and Russian are strong, but my English still has a long way to go. And I've never cooked a full meal by myself. I always end up calling my mother.

What excites me most about the future is the possibility of combining sport and science. I've already applied for a master's degree in sports science. If I get in, I will be able to study exactly what I love — how the body and mind work together under pressure.

I'm proud of what I've achieved. But I'm more proud of the fact that I haven't given up — not when I was injured, not when the research was difficult, not when the volleyball felt impossible. That is the experience that defines me most: I've learned to keep going.
